title: Private: SAML relaystate mangled during KMS rewrap leading to silent RBAC fallback
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Summary: Several enterprise Private customers reported sudden permission drops after a scheduled KMS key rotation. Investigation shows that for a subset of SAML-based SSO flows the RelayState payload is being altered during the KMS rewrap path, which causes tenant-scoped role attributes to be lost. Consequence: RBAC engine falls back to legacy default binding for the session (least-privilege fails open path in some clusters), and audit events that would show explicit role grants are not emitted (audit omission).

Observed behavior:
- Customers saw transient 403s for actions they previously had access to; in some cases the UI returned benign errors but background tasks silently degraded.
- Internal audit dashboards show missing "grant" events for affected sessions during the rotation window.
- Reproduced in our staging Private cluster when KMS rewraps assertion tokens that exceed intermediate envelope size threshold.

Root cause hypothesis: During KMS asynchronous rewrap, we stream and reserialize the SAML assertion envelope. A legacy buffer path truncates or re-encodes RelayState when envelope size crosses 8KB boundary; the RelayState contains tenant role mappings in our SSO adapter. The rewrap code path did not preserve relay metadata encoding flags (UTF-8 vs base64) which caused the role attribute to be dropped downstream. Audit emission relies on the presence of those attributes and is skipped when attributes absent, resulting in both RBAC fallback and audit omission.

Scope: Private clusters only (customer-managed VPCs and on-prem agents). Estimated affected sessions: customers on runtime-1.24 -> 1.26 private images with KMS-provider v2 and SAML connector enabled; currently seen in 3 paying customers; theoretical exposure for all Private customers using SAML + KMS rewraps.

Success criteria:
- Immediate mitigation removes customer-facing 403s and restores normal RBAC bindings for active sessions.
- Patch ensures RelayState and role attributes are preserved across rewraps and that audit events are emitted even when attributes are missing (explicit fail and alert path).
- Add e2e regression tests and monitoring to detect any future RelayState mutation or missing-audit events.

Proposed fix (high level):
1) Hotpatch: Update rewrap streaming code to bypass legacy buffer path and use the new envelope-preserve serializer when envelope size > 4KB. Add explicit re-encoding step: if RelayState is base64-encoded, persist encoding metadata and reapply after rewrap.
2) Emit an explicit audit event (audit:event=assertion-rewrap-attr-missing) when role attributes are absent post-unwrap, and surface a high-severity alert to oncall.
3) Add a canary rollout for Private control plane to validate behavior on 1 customer cluster before wide rollout.
4) Add unit and integration tests exercising boundary sizes and encoding permutations.

Rollback plan: Revert hotpatch and enable the previous synchronous KMS path (slower) if fix causes regressions. Advertise brief event window and coordinate with affected customers for a controlled revert.
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy private control plane with SAML connector + KMS provider v2 and configure tenant role attributes to be included in RelayState.
Generate a large SAML assertion (payload > 8KB) that triggers the rewrap streaming path during KMS rotation.
Trigger a KMS rotation (simulate rewrap) and observe resulting session attributes returned to the RBAC engine.
Inspect audit log for missing 'grant' or 'role-binding' events for the affected session window.
mitigation_notes: Temporary mitigation: disable asynchronous rewrap for affected customer clusters (control plane flag: kms.rewrap.async=false) to force synchronous path while hotpatch is validated.
Apply conservative canary that only enables the new serializer for clusters with SAML size > 4KB; communicate to customers the short maintenance window as needed.
Customer comms: point-of-contact assigned to SEs; notify impacted customers with remediation steps and offer follow-up runbook review.
resolution_plan: Day 0 (now): create and publish a hotpatch binary for runtime-1.26-private that uses envelope-preserve serializer. Push to one canary tenant cluster.
Day 1: if canary is green for 12h, roll to all affected Private clusters in waves with 30-minute health checks and audit verification.
Day 2-5: backfill tests and add alerting rule for 'assertion-rewrap-attr-missing' with SLA to page security on first occurrence.
Follow-up: include specifics in Private deployment upgrade notes and add to runbook for future KMS provider upgrades.
